disobedient and hard of hearing; how did faithful Zion, full of judgment, become a prostitute city; formerly righteousness was asleep in it, now it is murderous; it marvels at the wretched and unfavorable change of the Jews; the law through Moses was once a guide for what is beneficial, and the word of God was a shining and renowned leader, but now it is devoid of prophets, priests, and righteous works, and has abandoned the fear and love of God, and before the coming of our Savior, it prostrated itself to idols, and was utterly corrupted

Behold what the house of Israel has done to me, it went upon every high mountain and under every leafy tree and committed fornication there. And again to her: If a man sends away his wife and she goes from him and becomes another man's, will she return to him? That woman will be defiled. You have committed fornication with many shepherds and uncovered yourself before me, says the Lord. Lift up your eyes and see where you have not been ravished, you sat on the roads for them like a solitary crow in the wilderness. You have polluted the land with your fornications and evils, and you had many shepherds to stumble. Your appearance has become that of a prostitute, you have become shameless before all. For, as I said, despising the servitude under God, it turned to apostasy and unclean spirits and the servants of idols, using shepherds and teachers. And these, as I said, were the crimes of the Jewish synagogue before the sojourn of our Savior. But since Christ has shone upon those on the earth, it did not use him as a teacher, but rather valued teachings and commandments.
pass_b_english: …disobedient and hard of hearing; how did faithful Zion, full of judgment, become a prostitute city; formerly righteousness was asleep in it, now it is murderous. It marvels at the Jews' transition, which is a wretched and not a regular change, a movement from the better to the worse, and a transition from the unashamed to the shameful. For through Moses, the law once provided a knowledge of what is beneficial, and having a minister of the word of God for every practical matter, it was shining, most prosperous, and worthy, being distinguished among most men, to whom the fruit of righteousness was richly produced, and it was acceptable to God. For there were in it both prophets and priests, and those who meditated on the works of righteousness, and leaders of the people guarding judgment, having the law upon the tongue, and being instructed in every way both kind and good.

Now, being deprived of such things, it has instead fallen into the folly of abandoning that ancient moderation, and has been laid low by nothing less than the abandonment of its fear toward God and its love; and before the arrival of our Savior, it prostrated itself to those who are not gods by nature, utterly violating the one and true Lord through fornications directed toward this. Like a woman who is much-frequented and has been revered, she has acted impiously in many ways. At various times, she has been attached to different teachers, possessing the knowledge of conveying whatever has been preached by God. Indeed, she is accused through the voice of Jeremiah, the God of all things, saying: 'Behold what the house of Israel has done to me; it has gone upon every high mountain and under every leafy tree, and has committed fornication there' (Jeremiah 3:6).

And again to her: 'If a man sends away his wife, and she, having gone from him, becomes a man's other, will she not still be called to him? Will that woman not be defiled? You have committed fornication with many shepherds, and you have not uncovered yourself before me, says the Lord. Lift up your eyes to the straight way, and see where you have not been ravished; you sat upon the roads to them, like a solitary crow in the wilderness. You have polluted the land with your fornications and your evils, and you have had many shepherds as a stumbling block to yourself. The appearance of a prostitute has become yours; you have become shameless before all' (Jeremiah 3:12-24).

For, as I have said, despising the servitude under God, it turned toward apostasy and toward unclean spirits and toward the healers of idols, using shepherds and teachers. And these, as I have said, were the crimes of the Jewish Synagogue before the arrival of our Savior. But since Christ has shone upon those on the earth (for God the Lord has appeared to us, according to what is written), it did not use him more as a teacher; rather, it valued teachings and commandments…
